Variants.Content: Bolozo is located on the west bank of the rivers Pentos and Rhoyne, and is politically within the city-state of Pentos and its trade route network. It is a town, a center where surrounding populations, markets, roads and local power converge. Walls and roads tied the surrounding population, storage, and garrison here; even if the flags were changed, this stronghold would still affect how nearby people paid taxes, traded, and sought refuge.
Entry Bolozo Local families also rely on water, roads, arable land, herds, and markets where goods can be exchanged; if any road, well, or dock fails, the price falls first on them.

Entry Bolozo They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the known world; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but real distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hoof.

Entry Bolozo If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

The craftsmen use their hands to measure the workshops, markets, roof tiles, church bells and streets that have expanded through the ages in Poirozzo. The priests use rituals to continue the local gods, ancestral tombs and taboos passed down from generation to generation. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Bolozo They care about water sources, roads, cultivated land, herds, and markets where goods can be exchanged. They also look at whether seeds are left after harvesting grain and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
